title: The Fake KYC SMS
description: You receive an SMS saying your bank KYC has expired and your account will be blocked. What do you do?

content.title: New SMS
content.body: ALERT: Your Nova Bank KYC has expired. Your account will be BLOCKED within 24 hours. Update KYC immediately: novabank-kyc-update.in/verify

actions.label: Tap the link
actions.commentary: You opened a link from an unknown sender. Let us see what happens.

actions.label: Ignore the message
actions.commentary: Good thinking! Ignoring suspicious messages is a safe choice.

actions.label: Check the sender number
actions.commentary: Smart move! Checking who sent the message is an important first step.

content.title: Nova Bank — KYC Update
content.body:
Your account is at risk. Enter your details below to update your KYC and prevent account blocking.

Full Name: ___
Account Number: ___
Debit Card Number: ___
CVV: ___
OTP (sent to your mobile): ___

actions.label: Fill in the form
actions.commentary: You entered personal banking details on an unverified website.

actions.label: Check the website URL carefully
actions.commentary: Good catch! Let us look at this URL more carefully.

actions.label: Close the browser
actions.commentary: Good decision. Closing a suspicious page protects you.

content.title: Checking the details
content.body:
You notice:
• The sender is a random mobile number, not 'NOVBNK' (the official SMS header)
• The URL is 'novabank-kyc-update.in' — the real bank website is 'novabank.co.in'
• Real banks never ask for CVV or OTP via SMS links

This looks suspicious!

actions.label: Delete the message and block the number
actions.commentary: Excellent! Deleting and blocking prevents future scam attempts from this number.

actions.label: Call your bank's official number to verify
actions.commentary: Perfect choice. Calling the official number is the safest way to verify.

content.title: Account compromised (simulated)
content.body:
In a real scenario, the scammer now has your bank details. They could:
• Make unauthorised transactions
• Change your account password
• Apply for loans in your name

Do not worry — this was just practice. Let us learn what to do if this happens for real.

content.title: Safe choice!
content.body:
You avoided the scam by not clicking the link. Remember:
• Banks never send KYC links via SMS
• Real banks use registered SMS headers (like NOVBNK), not mobile numbers
• When in doubt, call your bank directly using the number on your card

content.title: Excellent awareness!
content.body: You identified the scam, deleted the message, and blocked the sender. You are well-prepared to handle this type of scam in real life.

content.title: Bank confirms it is a scam
content.body: Nova Bank's customer care confirms: 'We never send KYC update links via SMS. This is a known scam. Please do not click such links and report them to cybercrime.gov.in.'

actions.label: Report to cybercrime portal
actions.commentary: Reporting helps protect others from the same scam.

content.title: Recovery Steps
content.body:
If you shared your bank details on a suspicious website:

1. Call your bank immediately and request to block your card
2. Change your internet banking and UPI passwords
3. File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930
4. Monitor your account for unauthorised transactions
5. Visit your bank branch with ID proof to get a new card

Act within the first few hours for the best chance of recovery.
